messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: enterprise tenant 'Arbiter' experiencing elevated 5xx from eu-west endpoints. Error rate > 25% last 5m. Paging SRE oncall.@maya :rotating_light:
maya: Oncall acked — looking. Can someone paste the tenant & pool IDs?
liam: I see spikes in the arbiter-vpc dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-7e9a). Metrics: qps steady, tail latency OK, but error ratio jumping for model endpoints behind the eu-west gateway.
priya: Confirmed. Traces show DNS timeouts and a few connection resets from one eu-west AZ (eu-west-1b). Possibly a regional network flap to the dedicated pool.
nathan: Reached out to Arbiter account team to inform customer and gather any config changes on their side. Seeding: they reported intermittent request failures starting ~2851234400.
eva: Quick ask — do we have warm capacity in eu-west ready for a cutover? We can shift traffic to warm pool in eu-central if needed.
maya: Yes, we have warm capacity reserved: warm-pool-eu-west-standby (3 nodes), warm-pool-eu-central (5 nodes). Priority is to keep within their SLA.
liam: Plan proposal: 1) Drain traffic from faulty AZ by updating LB weights; 2) If errors persist, perform DNS cutover to eu-central warm pool with low TTL override; 3) If DNS not viable, do routing-level shift via SmartRouter fallback to dedicated pool in eu-central.
priya: +1. I'll prepare rollout steps and a canary. Suggest canary at 1% for 2 minutes, then 10%, then full. Also add auto-fallback on error spike > 10% in canary window.
maya: nathan, please confirm comms. liam/priya, list commands and who executes. I'll act as incident commander.
nathan: Messaging to Arbiter sent: "We're investigating increased 5xx; possible regional failover planned. We'll avoid full cutover until we validate warm pool." They acknowledged and requested minimized TTL changes.
liam: Executing AZ drain now: updating LB targets to remove eu-west-1b nodes for arbiter-vpc pool. Command:
```
# remove targets (example)
redwood lb update-targets --pool dp-7e9a --remove-node eu-west-1b-03
```
liam: Done. Monitoring error rate.
priya: Observing initial improvement but errors still ~8% (was 25%). Some clients still hitting GC-heavy nodes — probably cached DNS entries.
maya: Move to TTL override. We'll reduce Arbiter DNS TTL for the affected record to 30s, then issue DNS cutover to eu-central warm pool IP set. Priya, liam, get ready to rollback.
priya: Preparing DNS change: current CNAME -> arbiter-eu-west.rwd.io. New CNAME -> arbiter-eu-central-warm.rwd.io. Steps: 1) set TTL 30s; 2) after propagation (~60s) change CNAME; 3) monitor the 1% canary; 4) ramp.
nathan: Arbiter asked for a maintenance window note — I told them we'll keep them updated every 5m during the cutover.
liam: Starting TTL update now. Command:
```
# set TTL low
redwood dns update --record arbiter-prod --ttl 30
```
liam: TTL change propagated to authoritative. Waiting 60s before CNAME swap.
priya: Initiating canary (1%) to eu-central warm pool now. Router rule: set weight for arbiter->eu-central-warm = 0.01.
priya: Canary metrics: 1% saw 0.4% errors, latency comparable. No regression.
maya: Ramp to 10% after 2m.
priya: Ramp to 10% done. Monitoring: errors trending down to 1.2% overall.
liam: CNAME swap initiated now. Command:
```
redwood dns swap --record arbiter-prod --target arbiter-eu-central-warm.rwd.io
```
liam: Swap complete. Observing clients honoring new CNAME gradually.
priya: Traffic ramp to 50% then 100% over next 3m. Watch for tokenization/kv cache issues in model servers. We should warm KV caches first — issuing warm requests to new pool.
priya: Warming caches via replay: `redwood replay --tenant arbiter --pool warm-pool-eu-central --samples 1000`
priya: Cache warmup successful. No model errors.
maya: Customer impact update: initial 25% 5xx, after AZ drain and DNS cutover errors reduced to <1.5%. We'll keep monitoring for 30m and then close if stable. Nathan, please add a short incident note to Arbiter CS ticket.
nathan: Added note and scheduled follow-up sync. Arbiter said they saw intermittent failures stop ~2851234620, thanked ops.
eva: Postmortem actions I propose: - investigate root cause network flap in eu-west-1b with infra team - add health-check routing to reduce DNS TTL reliance - verify warm pool auto-warm timing for Arbiter-like workloads
maya: Agreed. I'll open a postmortem and assign owners. Closing actions: verify no residual routing rules, reset DNS TTL back to 300 after 30m stable, and document the canary thresholds used.
liam: Resetting LB targets to baseline and verifying node health.
nathan: Final customer update sent: "Traffic shifted, service restored, postmortem to follow." They marked ticket as acknowledged.
maya: Incident resolved for now. Will keep thread open for any regressions. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: arbiter tenant regional failover completed. Duration: ~8m.
